2xtp4 K5.routing: No router: each load stream targets one replica directly; the two replicas receive paired streams with identical inputs and seeds

engines.note: --num-gpu-blocks-override 399442 sets KV capacity equal to the K5 engine's 40,819,149 tokens; without it the engine would allocate 437,455 blocks

2xtp4 NoSpec (Window A+, replica 1 only).routing: Paired with K5 on replica 0: same inputs and seeds, run at the same time

dep8 K5.routing: Two load streams with distinct cache namespaces and request IDs share the one engine; vLLM data-parallel scheduling places requests

kv_capacity_source: GPU KV cache size in tokens as printed by each engine at startup (vLLM kv_cache_utils log line)
image_note: DSpark, --engram-config, --enable-scale-out, --per-request-spec-decode-metrics and the DSV41 attention backends are used as shipped in the pinned nightly image; their status in released vLLM is not tracked here

producer_code_sha256.note: All 128 measured units recorded the same three client hashes. Producer code is retained privately.

trace_replay_control.tool: vllm bench serve from the pinned image
trace_replay_control.prompt_construction: TimedTrace._sample_token in vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py samples token IDs uniformly from the vocabulary (special tokens removed) for each prefix-hash chunk
trace_replay_control.temperature_top_p: not set by the client (server defaults)
trace_replay_control.trace_source: a private 15-minute trace of request timings, prompt and output lengths and prefix-hash IDs; not published

speculative_decoding: DSpark static K5: five draft tokens per step, adaptive verification disabled, probabilistic draft sampling, block rejection sampling
client_cpus: 0-7,80-87 reserved for clients (server CPUs listed per engine)

measurement.arrivals: Turn 0 of each conversation is sent open-loop on a Poisson schedule; later turns of a conversation are sent back-to-back after the previous turn completes
measurement.measured_population: Conversations whose first turn is scheduled in the 360 s measured period; all their turns count, including turns finishing during drain
measurement.measured_arrivals: Measured conversations / 360 s, from the realized arrival schedule, reported per stream and per node; the generator's rate label is kept only as an identifier. In windows that did not stop early every scheduled first turn was dispatched
measurement.input_tokens_per_second: Offered prompt load: prepared prompt tokens of all scheduled measured turns / 360 s, including cached prefix. Matches server-reported prompt tokens within 0.0005% in every window where all turns completed
measurement.early_overload_stop: Stop after 120 s with a continuously nonempty engine waiting queue, or at once if more than 256 requests are waiting; unsent and unfinished turns count as misses

pass_rule.population: All scheduled measured turns; a turn that does not finish counts as infinite latency
pass_rule.dep8: Both streams pooled, shared queue empty after both streams finish, common drain deadline
pass_rule.quality_flags: Length-capped and repetition-flagged turns count as finished; flags are reported separately

sampling.seed: Per request, derived from the cell's seed label and request ID; identical across paired arms
sampling.tools: 12 function definitions offered on every request
sampling.cache_namespace: Each cell uses its own cache_salt, so prefix caching is shared within a cell (across turns of a conversation) and not across cells

populations.label 0.3: schedule applied to the 0.45 population's conversations
populations.midpoint labels: schedule applied to the 1.35 population's conversations (tokenized November 20)
populations.mean_prompt_tokens_per_conversation: per cell in tables/arms.csv as input_tokens_per_second x 360 / measured_conversations

populations.labels 0.12, 0.16 and midpoint: schedule applied to the 0.32 population's conversations (tokenized November 17)
populations.mean_prompt_tokens_per_conversation: per cell in tables/arms.csv as input_tokens_per_second x 360 / measured_conversations

workloads.lineage: All populations use the same input profile and public text; they differ only in which conversations were drawn. Deriving a lower-rate schedule from a larger population reuses tokenized requests without re-tokenizing
workloads.transcripts: Earlier assistant turns come from a frozen transcript, so generated answers do not change later prompts
